Synopsis

Mistral's PyPI SDK and npm SDK packages appeared in the May 2026 Shai-Hulud wave. The affected releases carried campaign loaders through official package distribution paths.

Story

The PyPI side of Shai-Hulud used a different shape from the npm worm. Instead of a `preinstall` script, `mistralai@2.4.6` placed its loader in `mistralai/client/__init__.py`, where ordinary imports could trigger it.

JFrog also listed Mistral npm SDK packages in the May 2026 Shai-Hulud appendix. Those artifacts are kept in this Mistral-scoped record so the campaign aggregates by vendor rather than by a broad catch-all package list.

The observed payload family targeted developer workstations and CI/CD runners. It searched for local files, cloud provider credentials, Kubernetes material, Vault tokens, password managers, and developer tooling secrets.

This record is scoped to Mistral SDK package distribution. The broader campaign record carries the cross-ecosystem TeamPCP/Shai-Hulud machinery and propagation behavior.
